# Design: NPC & Creature Power Framework

<!-- generated by /pingpong-solution on 2026-09-14 -->

## Problem & Intent
SagaDrive needs compact NPC/creature statblocks that use the same core rules as characters without forcing full character creation. The system must make level/power understandable to GMs, support ordinary enemies through solo bosses, and keep any creature promotable into a full playable character later.

## Non-Goals
- No separate combat ruleset for NPCs.
- No Minion tier in V1; weak enemies use lower levels.
- No generic attack/defense bonus merely for being Elite/Boss.
- No full encounter-budget implementation in this slice.
- No PC archetype/background reconstruction for compact statblocks.

## Assumptions
- Level remains 1-20.
- NPC/creature level band is shown as Machtgrad: 1-4 Gering, 5-8 Mittel, 9-12 Hoch, 13-16 Extrem, 17-20 Legendaer.
- Standard/Elite/Boss is a combat role for compact statblocks, not narrative importance, creature type, ownership, or controller.
- Full characters use normal character rules and do not intrinsically gain Standard/Elite/Boss modifiers.
- Compact statblocks use the same six attributes, skills, checks, defense, resistances, conditions, damage classes, and combat rules as the Core.

## Options Considered

### Option A: YAGNI - Level only
Use only level/profile, no Standard/Elite/Boss.
- Pros: minimal rules.
- Cons: does not solve solo-boss action economy or distinguish a normal wolf from an alpha/boss at the same level.
- Decision: rejected.

### Option B: Numeric tier bonuses
Elite/Boss gain global bonuses to attack, defense, saves, damage, and HP.
- Pros: simple to calculate; similar to quick elite adjustments in PF2e.
- Cons: displayed level stops meaning what it says, bounded numbers inflate, and bosses become frustrating through misses rather than interesting actions.
- Decision: rejected.

### Option C: Durability + bounded extra action economy - RECOMMENDED
Level/profile determine accuracy, defense, resistance, skill and base damage. Combat role changes durability, statblock complexity, and limited interleaved actions only.
- Pros: preserves level meaning, makes solo bosses viable, avoids raw-number inflation, stays readable.
- Cons: introduces one NPC-only interleaved-action concept.
- Evidence: PF2e explicitly uses top-down creature building and level benchmarks; Savage Worlds separates named/important Wild Cards from Extras while retaining shared traits; modern D&D statblocks optimize for at-table readability.

## Decision
**Chosen:** Option C.

### Shared rules
- `level`: 1-20; exact mechanical power anchor.
- `machtgrad`: display-only mapping from level:
  - 1-4 Gering
  - 5-8 Mittel
  - 9-12 Hoch
  - 13-16 Extrem
  - 17-20 Legendaer
- `combatRole`: `standard | elite | boss` for compact statblocks.
- `combatProfile`: `balanced | tough | offensive | mobile | ranged | control_support`.
- Combat role does **not** modify attack bonus, defense, resistances, skill modifiers, or base damage. Those come from level + profile + explicit abilities/equipment.
- Compact statblocks have no Drive/Momentum by default.
- At 0 HP a compact statblock is defeated/out of the conflict; the GM narrates dead, unconscious, destroyed, fled, etc. Full characters use normal dying rules.

### Health
Start from the normal SagaDrive base-health calculation / generated Standard benchmark.
- Standard: `100%` base HP.
- Elite: `150%` base HP, round up.
- Boss: `250%` base HP, round up.

### Standard
Target: ordinary individual at its level; designed to work well in groups.
- Normal turn: 1 main action, movement, interaction, 1 reaction.
- No extra interleaved action.
- Content guideline: 1-2 primary combat actions, 0-2 signature traits/abilities, optional normal reaction.
- Same-level balancing target: 1 threat unit.

### Elite
Target: roughly two ordinary enemies of the same level without simply raising accuracy/defense.
- HP: 150%.
- Normal turn unchanged.
- **Elite-Impuls: 1/round**, used after another figure finishes its turn; never during the Elite's own turn.
- One Elite-Impuls can either:
  1. move up to half normal movement, respecting all movement restrictions, or
  2. use one statblock ability explicitly tagged `Elite-Impuls`.
- An offensive Elite-Impuls is a minor attack/effect and should not exceed one damage class below the creature's primary attack unless the ability has an explicit balancing cost/condition.
- Maximum one interleaved impulse after any single other turn.
- Content guideline: 1-2 primary actions, 2-4 signature traits/abilities, at least one useful Elite-Impuls option.
- Same-level balancing target: 2 threat units.

### Boss
Target: central solo or near-solo opponent against multiple PCs.
- HP: 250%.
- Normal turn unchanged.
- **Boss-Impuls: 2/round**, each used after another figure finishes its turn; maximum one after any single other turn.
- Each Boss-Impuls can either:
  1. move up to half normal movement, respecting restrictions, or
  2. use one statblock ability tagged `Boss-Impuls`.
- Boss-Impuls attacks/effects are deliberately minor; the Boss's full-power signature actions remain main actions on its own turn.
- **Wendepunkt: 1/combat**. Every Boss statblock defines one explicit phase/change trigger, normally the first time it reaches 50% max HP. The effect must be written in the statblock (terrain change, reposition, summon, stance change, new attack pattern, etc.). There is no generic condition cleanse or automatic immunity.
- Content guideline: 1-2 primary attacks, 3-5 signature traits/abilities, at least two Boss-Impuls options, exactly one Wendepunkt definition.
- Same-level balancing target: 4 threat units.

### Conditions and restrictions
- Combat role grants no blanket immunities or "legendary resistance".
- Existing conditions still work normally.
- `Kampfunfaehig` prevents Elite-/Boss-Impulse use.
- Movement impulses obey `Gegriffen`, terrain, movement mode, and other normal restrictions.
- Impulses are not reactions and do not consume the normal reaction; only abilities explicitly tagged for them may be used.

### Full character boundary
- Standard/Elite/Boss modifiers belong to compact-statblock combat construction, not to the identity/controller of a full character.
- `Compact -> Full` removes the compact combat-role overlay and produces a legal full SagaDrive character.
- A later adventure/session slice may apply an encounter-specific boss overlay to a full NPC, but that is not intrinsic character data.

## UI Contract
Creator shows:
1. Stufe 1-20.
2. Derived Machtgrad label.
3. `Kampfrolle`: Standard / Elite / Boss, with helper text that this changes durability/action economy, not narrative importance.
4. Kampfprofil.
5. Live statblock preview.

Example card/meta: `Stufe 7 · Machtgrad Mittel` / `Elite · Zäh` / `Statblock`.

Standard/Elite/Boss explanatory copy:
- Standard: "Normale Ausfuehrung dieser Stufe. Gut fuer Gruppen und gewoehnliche Gegner."
- Elite: "Besonders widerstandsfaehig und aktiver im Konflikt. Ziel: etwa zwei Standards derselben Stufe."
- Boss: "Zentraler Einzelgegner mit zusaetzlichen Boss-Impulsen und einem Wendepunkt. Ziel: etwa vier Standards derselben Stufe."

## Cross-Domain Sign-Off
| Domain | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| KISS | ✅ | Three roles; no Minion tier; no second combat system. |
| SOLID | ✅ | Combat-role overlay is separate from identity/controller/full-character model. |
| DRY | ✅ | Reuses Core stats, damage classes, conditions, actions and derived values. |
| Security | ✅ | Pure rules/data decision; no new trust boundary. |
| UI/UX | ✅ | Level + derived Machtgrad + plain-language combat role hides benchmark math. |
| Scaling | ✅ | Pure deterministic calculation; no service dependency. |
| Testability | ✅ | HP multipliers, impulse limits and role invariants are deterministic. |
| Maintainability | ✅ | Role does not alter accuracy/defense formulas, reducing cross-system coupling. |

## Confidence
**95%** - product intent is confirmed, current Core combat formulas and architecture are mapped, and the remaining uncertainty is numerical playtest tuning rather than model structure.

## Implementation Sketch
Affected paths for the future implementation issue:
- `docs/sagadrive core rules.md` - normative compact NPC/creature rules.
- `src/domains/rules/sagadrive/**` - pure combat-role/benchmark contracts and calculations.
- `src/domains/npc-creature/**` (or final domain name after issue #2 architecture decision) - compact definition contract.
- unit/regression scripts - role invariants and benchmark tests.

New dependencies: none.
Tests: rules-kernel unit/regression tests; later verify-ui in creator issue.
